title: Understanding Sampling Distributions
text: When you take multiple samples from a population and calculate the mean of each sample, the distribution of these sample means tends to form a specific shape. What shape do you think this is?

title: Central Limit Theorem Insight
text: The Central Limit Theorem tells us something important about the distribution of sample means, especially as the sample size increases. How does this theorem describe the shape of the distribution?

hintAnswer: A histogram of $$10000$$ sample means from samples of size $$n=1000$$.
title: Sample Size and Distribution Shape
text: Consider the effect of sample size on the distribution of sample means. Which of the following is most likely to resemble a normal distribution?
choices: A histogram of $$10000$$ sample means from samples of size $$n=1000$$.
A histogram of incomes from a SRS of $$n=10000$$ households.
A histogram of incomes from the entire census.
None of these would resemble a normal distribution.
